subject: setting initial values in R Distance

messages.author: 3314d7ad28eab19e
messages.subject: setting initial values in R Distance
parts:
Dear Group,

I have been fitting several distance models, attempting to find the best-fitting detection function for my data. I am including 1-2 covariates and I have to bin the data into 4 intervals since there was apparent rounding (e.g. at 500m, 1000m, etc.) in the distance data. The problem I'm having seems to be a common one: the hazard-rate key function fails to converge on estimates with 2nd order (or higher) adjustment and only 1 covariate. I've scaled the covariate, which does not help. The hazard-rate model still reports an AIC estimate which suggests it is the best model (compared to half-normal or uniform), and the plotted distance function looks like a good fit to my data. However, I'd still like to see a model without the convergence error.

I've reviewed the guidance on setting initial values and bounds (e.g. https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/mrds/versions/2.1.17/topics/mrds-opt), but it still isn't clear to me how to specify the initial values within the script. Can anyone provide a basic example? My current code is as follows...

cutpoints = seq(0,2000,by=500)
hr.m5 = ds(dat, truncation=2000, transect="point", cutpoints=cutpoints, formula = ~ viewshed, key="hr", adj="cos", order=c(2))

Thanks in advance for your help.
best,
Shawn

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] setting initial values in R Distance
parts:
Shawn

Here is the answer to the question you asked:

There is an argument in ds() called "initial.values", which is a named list.  Here is an example of its use in conjunction with the rmarkdown file of minke whale sightings provided at http://distancesampling.org/R/vignettes/minke.Rmd

whale.pooledf0 <- ds(whales, truncation=whale.trunc,
                        key="hr", 
                       initial.values=list(scale=-0.2, shape=2.0, adjustment=0.2),
                       adjustment="cos", order=c(2))

Here is the answer to the question you didn't ask.

You are cutting your data into 4 bins (0-500, 500-1000, 1000-1500, 1500-2000); that equals the points of support for the model you are fitting.  To those points of support you are fitting a 2-parameter hazard rate model, with a covariate and a cosine adjustment.  It is no surprise that you will get convergence errors because you are fitting a model with four parameters to four points of support.  In addition, there is likely to be strong correlation between the parameter estimates, leading to yet more drama for the optimisation software.

I made the comment on 08June to another query (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/distance-sampling/5L7KufGx6x4) suggesting that covariates and adjustment terms are somewhat redundant in their tasks.  I would be quite surprised if both are necessary for data binned to four bins.
